# Respira

> Respira is a free iOS app for pollen and air-quality tracking. It shows the current pollen level for a species and location, a short forecast, and a symptom diary. Available in 35 countries: 29 in Europe (Spain, Portugal, France, Italy, Germany, Ireland, the UK, Austria, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Greece, Croatia, Romania, Bulgaria, Serbia) on the Copernicus CAMS model, and the US, Japan, Australia, New Zealand, Argentina and Chile on the Google Pollen API.

Pollen data for Spain and the rest of Europe comes from the CAMS atmospheric model (Copernicus) via Open-Meteo, refreshed once daily; species without model coverage fall back to a seasonal estimate from the Spanish Aerobiology Network (REA), always labeled as such. Pollen data for the US, Japan, Australia, New Zealand, Argentina and Chile comes from the Google Pollen API; in Japan the app also shows, in season, the previous day's measured counts from the Ministry of the Environment's pollen survey. Every page states its own source and last-updated time — nothing here should be read as a live measurement unless the page says so.

## App

- [Respira on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/6759206565): free, iPhone and iPad, pollen levels, forecast, symptom diary, no ads on Respira Pro.

## Start here

- [Respira in English](https://respiraapp.fit/en/): what the app does and the 35 countries it covers.
- [Respira en español](https://respiraapp.fit/): today's pollen and air quality in Spain's main cities.

## Free tools

- [Pollen calendar for your city (English)](https://respiraapp.fit/en/pollen-calendar): pick a city and your allergies to see the months each pollen is usually at moderate or above, this month and what comes next. 19 UK and Irish cities from the Copernicus CAMS model (2023-2025 average), 50 US cities from Respira's regional seasonal calendars (estimates, labelled as such).
- [Pollen food allergy (English)](https://respiraapp.fit/en/pollen-food-allergy): which fruits, vegetables and nuts are linked to eight pollens (birch, alder, grass, olive, mugwort, ragweed, cypress, plane tree), the protein behind each link and whether cooking helps, every fact sourced (EAACI Molecular Allergology User's Guide 2.0 and journal studies). Not a diagnosis.
- [Alergia cruzada entre polen y alimentos (Spanish)](https://respiraapp.fit/alergia-cruzada-polen-alimentos): the same, in Spanish.
- [Calendario polínico de tu ciudad (Spanish)](https://respiraapp.fit/calendario-polen): the same tool for Spain's 52 provincial capitals: the CAMS model's 2023-2025 average for grass, olive, birch, alder, mugwort and ragweed, and the Spanish Aerobiology Network's calendar for the five species the model does not carry.

## Pollen by city — United States (English)

- [50 US cities](https://respiraapp.fit/en/pollen-map-usa): month-by-month calendar and what's in season right now, one page per city.

## Pollen by city — United Kingdom and Ireland (English)

- [19 UK and Ireland cities](https://respiraapp.fit/en/pollen-map-uk-ireland): today's level by type (grass, birch, alder, mugwort, ragweed) from the Copernicus CAMS model, a multi-day forecast and a 2023-2025 monthly calendar for each city, rebuilt daily.
- [Pollen in Australia](https://respiraapp.fit/en/pollen-australia): when grass pollen season runs south and north of 28°S and when cypress pine flowers, from Respira's seasonal calendar for Australia (an estimate, labelled as such), and what the app shows there (Google Pollen API, grass and cypress pine).
